Phase 1 · Two-part working checklist

Frame the Mandate

Two parts: macroeconomic analysis, then client submissions.

Part 1Macroeconomic AnalysisBuild and submit one documented 12-month macro forecast with three probability-weighted scenarios before applying it to the clients. Part 2Client SubmissionsReview each client’s criteria, consider risk, return, utility, and risk aversion, and explain asset allocation in one abbreviated IPS per client. Submit the three IPS statements together.

Decision question

What must be true about markets and each client before we are willing to invest?

Establish one defensible 12-month market view and convert each assigned client profile into an approved investment mandate.

Submit the macro forecast as Assignment 1. Use that forecast in Assignment 2 to complete the three client IPS statements. Each assignment has its own Canvas receipt.

Part 1 of 2

Macroeconomic Analysis

Build and submit one documented 12-month macro forecast with three probability-weighted scenarios before applying it to the clients.

Do this in order

  1. 1

    Open the Macro Starter workbook, assign all five roles, and save a team-named Part 1 copy.

  2. 2

    Complete the detailed macro analysis in the provided workbook: review historical evidence, form a human-first interpretation, and document sources.

  3. 3

    Compare the committee view with FRED historical observations and a source-dated FactSet or other external forecast or consensus where a comparable measure exists; then create bull, base, and bear scenarios with probabilities totaling 100%.

Ready when

  • The macro workbook documents historical analysis, source-dated external comparisons, inflation expectations, and weighted bull, base, and bear scenarios.

Evidence to keep

  • Human-first five-year macro read with source dates
  • Source-dated external forecast comparison, FRED historical evidence, and team growth, inflation, rate, and sentiment forecasts
  • Bull/base/bear scenarios with probabilities totaling 100%

Macro forecast deliverable

  • Completed macro starter workbook

Resources for this part

HTML Macro Forecast step-by-step guide Workbook-mapped steps for a human-first macro view, AI challenge, independent verification, scenarios, and the Part 1 submission. XLSX Macro starter workbook Source-dated historical data, human-first analysis, verified external comparisons, inflation expectations, and weighted bull/base/bear forecasts.

Assignment 1: submit the macro forecast

Complete and submit the macro starter workbook as the Part 1 group assignment. One designated team member submits for the group; every team member verifies the Canvas receipt. Carry the submitted forecast into Part 2 and document any later revision in the decision record.

  • BUS331_[TeamName]_Phase1_Macro.xlsxCompleted macro starter workbook with historical evidence, human-first read, source-dated consensus comparison, inflation forecast, and probability-weighted bull/base/bear scenarios.
Check this Canvas submission

Part 2 of 2

Client Submissions

Review each client’s criteria, consider risk, return, utility, and risk aversion, and explain asset allocation in one abbreviated IPS per client. Submit the three IPS statements together.

Do this in order

  1. 1

    Review your three assigned client profiles and data. Consider goals, constraints, risk capacity, risk willingness, target return, utility, and risk aversion.

  2. 2

    Complete one abbreviated IPS mandate per client. Explain how the client criteria and risk–return trade-off influence broad allocation weights totaling 100%, using the submitted macro outlook as context.

  3. 3

    Review the three abbreviated IPS statements together, check each allocation totals 100%, and submit one combined client IPS PDF.

Work from the assigned scenarios

Use the four-step client guide to review risk, return, utility, and risk aversion, then complete one abbreviated IPS per client. No client interviews are required.

Ready when

  • Each client has a completed abbreviated IPS with goals, relevant constraints, return and risk policies, and a provisional allocation totaling 100%.
  • Each IPS explains how risk, return, utility, and risk aversion influence the allocation, using the submitted macro outlook as context.
  • The team has checked all three IPS statements and combined them into one PDF in assigned-client order.

Evidence to keep

  • Client goals and relevant constraints recorded in all three abbreviated IPS statements
  • Risk, return, utility, and risk-aversion reasoning supporting each client’s allocation
  • Provisional broad allocation totaling 100% and concise return and risk policies for each client

Client and committee deliverables

  • Three completed abbreviated client IPS statements combined into one PDF

Assignment 2: submit the three client IPS statements

Review the supplied client profiles and data, discuss risk, return, utility, and risk aversion, and complete one abbreviated IPS per client. Combine all three IPS statements into one PDF in assigned-client order. Submit only this PDF for Part 2; no separate mandate memo, Decision Log, or Gate 1 vote is required. Use the macro forecast already submitted in Part 1 as context. No client interviews are required. One designated team member submits for the group; every member verifies the Canvas receipt.

Committee responsibilities across both parts

Committee seatResponsibility in Phase 1
Client and Macro StrategistLead analysis of the assigned client scenarios, document goals and RRTTLLU constraints, establish the macro context, and label reasoned assumptions and information gaps.
Fixed-Income AnalystTranslate cash-flow needs, time horizon, liquidity, taxes, and loss capacity into fixed-income questions and provisional guardrails.
Equity AnalystTranslate the client's growth needs, time horizon, values, tax position, liquidity, and concentration limits into equity-selection guardrails.
Portfolio ManagerReconcile risk capacity and willingness, coordinate the team’s allocation discussion, and check the three abbreviated IPS statements.
Risk and Derivatives AnalystDefine the downside questions, drawdown tripwire, stress priorities, and residual-risk evidence the final portfolio must address.

Ready for Phase 2

Check that the three abbreviated IPS statements reflect the clients’ criteria and provide usable return, risk, and allocation policies for Phase 2. No formal Phase 1 vote is required.
